mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions that reduce corporate investment and consumer spending.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return does not diverge from the pre-rates-rise period mean by at least one standard deviation, or the 5-day realized volatility of SPX does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 2% over three consecutive months is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak labor demand reduces consumer and business confidence.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in at least 70% of similar labor weak episodes, or the 5-day realized volatility of SPX is lower than during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) unexpectedly exceeds its prior quarter trend by at least 2%, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive as the surprise suggests resilient demand and economic momentum.
failure_condition: Over 100 similar positive surprise episodes, the average 60-day forward return does not exceed the mean of negative surprise episodes by one standard error.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals tight labor markets, prompting firms to accelerate capex and lift equity valuations, pushing the S&P 20-day forward return positive.
failure_condition: In 10 similar tightening regimes, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3.0 suggest the Fed is unlikely to raise rates, which supports a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as risk premia compress.
failure_condition: During 20 such episodes, the 5-day forward return mean is not higher than the mean during high-inflation episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When residential construction (HOUST) rises by more than 5% month-over-month for two consecutive months, it reflects renewed housing demand and economic optimism, which drives a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Across 50 such episodes, the 20-day forward return mean is not higher than the mean during neutral construction periods by one standard deviation.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both unemployment (UNRATE) and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 1% each month indicates dual weakening in labor and supply chains, which amplifies downside risk and produces a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < prev_month - 1% AND INDPRO < prev_month - 1% for 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: Dual weakening labor and supply shock
failure_condition: In 30 similar interaction episodes, the 20-day forward return mean is not more than one standard deviation below the mean of single-variable weak episodes.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of rising consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) but stable or declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 60-day forward return turns positive as labor market strength is interpreted as a sustainable growth signal rather than a price-stifling one.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > prev_month * 1.02 AND CPIAUCSL < prev_month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 40 such episodes, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically different from zero when isolated labor strength episodes are compared (p > 0.05).
